target_customer: Buyers of permanent carbon removal credits; at founding also cement and glass manufacturers wanting carbon-negative materials
problem: Atmospheric CO2 removal was costly and unverified; the founders aimed to remove CO2 permanently and cheaply by processing seawater into carbonates.
business_model: Sells permanent CO2 removal (carbon credits); originally also sale of limestone and carbonate materials
product_category: Carbon removal and direct air capture hardware

founders.name: Marcus Lima
education: Oxford and Cambridge graduate (degrees not specified on YC page)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says the idea came while he and Millar were in master's programs at Oxford.

founders.name: Erik Millar
education: BEng Mechanical Engineering, University of Oxford
MSc Energy Systems, University of Oxford
previous_startups: Carbon farming projects in Australia (outcome not stated)
Solar farm on the Isle of Man (outcome not stated)

technical_complexity.rationale: At founding the process of electrochemically treating seawater to make carbonates was shown only at lab scale per TechCrunch, and scaling to a pilot and then a DAC plant needed hardware and chemical engineering work.

defensibility.rationale: Process know-how and a first large operating plant in Oklahoma give some lead, but several DAC firms with far larger funding competed for the same credits.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying or buying Heimdal; the company opened its Bantam plant in Oklahoma in August 2024.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in Aug 2021 quotes Millar saying carbon markets that make removal economically viable had only just formed, and the company had letters of intent from cement and glass manufacturers.

branding.domain_note: Uses heimdalccu.com; the root URL returned a 404 when fetched.
branding.brand_signature: Affordable, Verified DAC slogan and the Bantam plant name
branding.community_and_virality: Bloomberg and E&E News covered the Bantam facility opening in August 2024, mostly about the project rather than the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: Press covered the plant, but the name overlaps with Heimdall Power and the Norwegian Heimdal carbon capture project, which crowd search results.

pivots.from: Making carbon-neutral building materials from seawater
pivots.to: Selling permanent CO2 removal through direct air capture
pivots.why: Not stated in the sources opened; a search summary says the model shifted exclusively to carbon removal

outcome_analysis: Heimdal raised a $6.4M seed in 2021, then pivoted from seawater materials to direct air capture and opened the Bantam plant in Oklahoma in August 2024, which counts as a milestone beyond most seed climate firms. YC lists the company as inactive, which conflicts with the evidence of an operating plant, so the label may be stale or reflect a later change not found in sources.
notes: YC status is Inactive but sources show Bantam operating from August 2024, so exit type is none and the conflict is flagged here. Total raised conflicts: CB Insights search summary says $17.47M with investors including Kiloton Fund, Parallel18 and BV IgniteX; sp-edge says $10.8M; employbl says $10.7M; Seedtable lists a $130K pre-seed in Aug 2021 and a separate $6M unknown-stage 2021 round, which matches the $6.4M seed; VCBacked says $40K. The recorded round is only the TechCrunch seed; a gap exists between $6.4M and the later totals, probably later rounds not found. The company website returned 404 on the root URL. TechCrunch named no competitors, and no source dated near the batch was found, so the list is empty.
